Mesial temporal lobe epilepsy is the most common cause of such semiology in adults, especially with automatisms (grimacing) and retrograde amnesia. Frontal lobe epilepsy is plausible given prominent motor features (facial twitching) and brief duration, though typically shorter (<2 min) and more stereotyped; supplementary motor area seizures can mimic temporal lobe semiology. Atypical absence epilepsy is unlikely in adulthood without prior history or generalized spike-wave on EEG; its typical duration is seconds, not minutes. TIA is low-probability: episodes are too brief for persistent deficits, lack vascular risk factors or lateralizing neurologic signs, and recurrence over a month contradicts typical TIA timing (usually isolated or clustered within hours/days)."}
